mainEntity.name: What does each body fat percentage look like?

acceptedAnswer.text: At 8% body fat, men show deep ab separation, vascularity, and striated muscle — stage-lean. At 13%, they show clear six-pack definition and an athletic build. 18% is a lean, fit look with some ab outline under good light. 23% is average — softer midsection, no visible abs. 28% shows a noticeable belly and love handles. 33% and above is classified as obese range with clinical health implications.

mainEntity.name: Does body fat distribution change with age?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Same body fat percentage looks different across decades. Men tend to lose muscle mass (sarcopenia) after age 40, so a 45-year-old at 18% body fat often looks softer than a 25-year-old at 18% because the underlying muscle base is smaller. Body fat also shifts toward the midsection with age due to hormonal changes.

mainEntity.name: What is a healthy body fat percentage for men?

acceptedAnswer.text: For men, the American Council on Exercise ranges are: athletes 6–13%, fitness 14–17%, average 18–24%, obese 25%+. Essential fat — the minimum your body needs to function — is 2–5% for men. Most health authorities recommend 10–20% for long-term health in adult men.

mainEntity.name: How do I measure my body fat percentage?

acceptedAnswer.text: DEXA scans are the gold standard at ±1–2% accuracy but cost $75–150 per session. The U.S. Navy tape-measure method is ±3–4% and free. Bioelectrical impedance scales are ±4–8% and heavily affected by hydration. AI photo analysis (like GainFrame) is ±2–3% trending and excels at tracking change over time from a single phone photo.
